landings.title: Family & Visit Visas for Qatari Investors
landings.headline: Family and Visit Visa Documentation Support for Qatari Residents in Dubai
landings.summary: Document preparation and application support for Qatari residents sponsoring family or inviting visitors: attested certificates, insurance and accommodation records.
landings.contentHtml:
Bringing family from Qatar

Qatari investors and companies use Dubai for trading, services and holding structures. Cross-border payments are simple because both currencies are pegged to the dollar, and Dubai's licensing system gives clear routes for foreign-owned companies. Many residents want to bring a spouse, children or parents to Dubai, or invite relatives and business visitors. We provide document preparation and application support; GDRFA and the ICP decide each case. The service is described in family and visit visa documentation.

Certificates issued in Qatar

Qatari documents are attested by the competent Qatari authority and by the UAE embassy where required. The exact steps depend on the document and change from time to time, so we confirm them before you start; Arabic documents may be accepted without translation. Sponsor requirements, such as income and accommodation, are set by the authorities and change, so we confirm them before you apply. Insurance for dependants is arranged through our insurance processing service.

Home-country points that affect this service

  • Qatari documents are attested by the competent Qatari authority and by the UAE embassy where required. The exact steps depend on the document and change from time to time, so we confirm them before you start; Arabic documents may be accepted without translation.
  • Transfers between Qatari and UAE banks are international payments. Banks ask for the purpose and the source of funds, and keeping your licence and agreement documents ready speeds up the review.

Documents and information to prepare

  • Sponsor's passport, residence visa and Emirates ID
  • Marriage and birth certificates issued in Qatar, attested and translated where required
  • A registered tenancy contract or ownership proof for the sponsor's accommodation
  • Passport copies and photographs for each family member
  • Valid health insurance for each dependant

How it works from Qatar

  1. We confirm the sponsor's eligibility and start attestation of certificates from Qatar.
  2. The application is prepared and submitted through the authorised channel.
  3. Family members complete medical fitness, biometrics and Emirates ID steps in the UAE.
  4. Insurance and the Ejari record are kept current for renewals.

Currency and payments

The Qatari riyal and the dirham are both pegged to the US dollar, so the riyal-dirham rate is stable for budgeting.

US documents are normally notarised and then apostilled or authenticated by the state Secretary of State, or by the US Department of State for federal documents, before any further step needed for UAE use. landings.headline: Company Formation in Dubai for French Investors
landings.summary: How French founders form a mainland or free zone company in Dubai: licence type, ownership, documents from France and the steps after the licence.
landings.contentHtml:
What company formation means for an French owner

French entrepreneurs and companies choose Dubai for business development, consulting, trading and hospitality ventures, and many keep commercial links with France. A clear structure and good records make the move to Dubai smoother. This page explains how the Dubai side of company formation works when the owners, directors or shareholders are based in France, and where your home country adds extra steps. The full service is described in our guide to company formation and business setup, and the country overview is in setting up in Dubai from France.

Mainland or free zone for owners in France

A mainland licence from the Department of Economy and Tourism lets the company trade across the UAE and rent premises in the city. A free zone licence is issued by the zone's own authority and often suits companies that serve customers outside the UAE. If your customers are mostly in France or other export markets, compare both before you choose; our DED and DET services page explains how the licence types differ.

Home-country points that affect this service

  • French tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income and must declare foreign accounts, and French rules on foreign entities may apply to a Dubai company. France and the UAE have a double tax agreement. Check your position with a French tax adviser first.
  • Payments from French banks to Dubai are international transfers in euro or dollars. Banks ask for the purpose and the source of funds, so keep contracts and capital documents ready.
  • French public documents carry an apostille issued by the competent authority, and notarial documents by the court of appeal for the notary's area. A sworn translation into Arabic or English is usually needed for UAE use.

Documents and information to prepare

  • Passport copies of every shareholder and manager (valid for at least six months is a common requirement)
  • Proof of address in France, such as a recent bank letter or utility bill, where the authority asks for it
  • For a corporate shareholder: certificate of incorporation, articles and a board resolution from France, attested for UAE use
  • Memorandum of Association, signed in Dubai or in front of a notary abroad with the correct attestation
  • Proposed trade name and a plain-language description of the activity

How it works from France

  1. Confirm the activity, ownership and number of visas, and choose mainland or a free zone.
  2. Sign the memorandum and any power of attorney, and attest documents from France (POA drafting, MOA drafting).
  3. Obtain initial approval, register the tenancy and submit the licence application.
  4. After the licence: corporate tax registration, residence files (visa support) and bank account documents.

Currency and payments

The dirham is pegged to the US dollar, not the euro, so the euro-dirham rate moves with the euro-dollar market. Budget for exchange-rate changes over the life of the project and compare transfer providers for larger amounts.

faqs.answer: Start with Invest in Dubai and the UAE Government Portal for licensing and the Dubai Land Department for tenancy registration. For your home rules, check the Dutch tax administration (Belastingdienst) and a Dutch tax adviser.
